notes: SAMPLE numbers: an invented study, not real. It only shows what the page looks like.
All dollar figures are estimates from past bets. Nothing here is a promise or advice to place a bet.
Paper-worthy needs at least 30 bets and a positive edge on the cautious (lower 95%) win rate, after fees.
Sizes: a quarter of Kelly, at most 2% of the bankroll per bet and 6% across the day's picks. Sibyl never places a bet; the Kalshi bot is untouched.
Monthly figure (estimate): the best pick's cautious dollars per bet times how often that kind of bet came up, times 30. One pick only: the picks overlap, so they are never added up.

risks.title: Edges that fade
risks.detail: 1 kinds of bet still show a cautious edge but the study marks them fading. Edges on Kalshi do not last.

risks.title: The bot is in a losing week
risks.detail: The Kalshi bot lost $6.70 over the last 7 days. A losing week is information: size down, not up.

risks.title: The picks overlap
risks.detail: Several picks are the same bets seen through different filters (a price band, a coin, a strategy). They win and lose together, so the day's risk is closer to one bet than to several. That is why the total is capped at 6% of the bankroll.

risks.title: Near-certain bets lose big
risks.detail: Buying at 95¢ and up wins most of the time and pays a few cents; one loss costs about twenty wins. A single bad day can erase weeks.

risks.title: Fees and fills
risks.detail: Kalshi's fee is already in the edge, but real orders can fill at a worse price than the study's average. Paper results are always a little kinder than real ones.

risks.title: Looking back is not a promise
risks.detail: Every number is history. Picks come from the same bets they are judged on; only the forward tally is out of sample, and it is small.
